reference_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.n_orders = 1 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS share_one_order
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t
alternatives:
SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.n_orders = 1) * 1.0 / COUNT(*), 3) AS share_one_order
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t

WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN n_orders = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*), 3) AS share_one_order
FROM customer_orders

other_way.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN n_orders = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*), 3) AS share_one_order
FROM customer_orders
other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step and an explicit count over count reads plainly; the average of a 1-or-0 flag is shorter but less obvious.
